findings.title: "anchor" is a homonym: a Markdown-heading anchor and a full-strength-hat/lane anchor share the bare word with no signal they differ
locations: src/CLI/Config.jl:113-119 (`resolve_anchor(root, anchor) -> (file, line, count)` — "Resolves a `file#heading` anchor")
src/CLI/Preflight.jl:193 (`anchor`, whether it runs at full strength rather than on the economy model (a `domain_hats` entry may anchor any key))
findings.description: A cold reader meets `anchor` for the first time in `Config.resolve_anchor`'s docstring (module #6 in the dependency-order read), where it unambiguously means a `file#heading` Markdown-heading reference used throughout the doctor and scan engine (`Scan.jl:245-246`, `Doctor.jl:239-241,283`). Many files later, `Preflight.resolve_hats` reuses the identical bare word `anchor` for a completely unrelated concept — a hat or lane that runs at full strength instead of the economy model. Neither docstring flags that these are two unrelated ideas sharing one name; a reader who has already bound `anchor` to "heading reference" will silently misread every later `anchor` field (`h["anchor"]`, `l["anchor"]`, `roster_record`'s `anchor` key, `Doctor.jl:274,278,281` "no anchored hat") as some kind of heading pointer rather than a full-strength flag. This is exactly the ordinary-English-word-with-a-second-package-meaning failure mode: it never trips an undefined-symbol check because the word IS defined — just for a different referent.
findings.resolution_hint: Rename one of the two concepts (e.g. call the full-strength flag `anchored`/`full_strength` instead of reusing `anchor`), or add an explicit disambiguating clause at the second use's first docstring (`Preflight.resolve_hats`): "`anchor` here is unrelated to `Config.resolve_anchor`'s heading anchors; it means...".

findings.title: "instrument" — a declared term of art — is used in nearly every docstring but never defined or enumerated anywhere in the source
locations: src/GBGCodingTools.jl:4 (module docstring: "the review instruments, the docs-build wrapper..." — first use, no definition)

src/DocLints.jl:11 (`makedocs` docstring: "the instruments whose open rounds gate the build (a round is one run of an instrument over the consumer...)" — defines ROUND using the undefined word INSTRUMENT)

src/CLI/Preflight.jl:516 (`- \`instrument\` — one of the four instruments.` — the closest thing to a definition anywhere in the corpus, and it is circular: it never names what the four are or what an instrument fundamentally is)
findings.description: `instrument` is one of the ten terms of art this package's own catalogue names, yet a search across every docstring in `src/` and `ext/` for a defining clause ("one of the four", "four instruments", "review procedure") turns up only the module docstring's bare mention and Preflight.jl's self-referential "one of the four instruments" — which itself never says what the four ARE. A cold reader who has read every module and function docstring in the package still cannot answer "what is an instrument?" from the docstrings alone; they can only infer it is used to classify rounds (`rec["instrument"]`, round ids `<date>-<instrument>-<NN>`) and gates their closure. This is the single most pervasive undefined term in the corpus — it recurs in `DocLints.jl`, `TestHarness.jl`, `Witnesses.jl`, `Scan.jl`, `Sync.jl`, `Ledger.jl`(comment), `Hunt.jl`, `Audit.jl`, `RoundFiles.jl`, `Gate.jl`, `Config.jl`, `Rounds.jl`, `Passes.jl`, `Fleet.jl`, `Release.jl` — with never a defining sentence.
findings.resolution_hint: State once, in the `GBGCodingTools` module docstring (its very first mention, alongside `consumer`) or in a dedicated docstring that others `@ref`-link: "An instrument is one of the four review procedures — `check-docs`, `check-consistency`, `bug-hunt`, `audit-changes` — each run as a round." Then `@ref`-link the first mention of `instrument` in every other file back to it (RULE.DOC.XLINK).

findings.title: "gate" denotes at least three distinct package objects plus the plain-English verb, none disambiguated or cross-linked at first use
locations: src/DocLints.jl:11,17-18 (`makedocs` docstring, file #3 read: "the instruments whose open rounds gate the build" then "the closure gate of the two docs instruments... the gate again" — first noun-sense use, no definition, no @ref)

src/TestHarness.jl:536-545 (`TestHarness.gate` docstring: "The closure gate a consumer's runtests.jl ends with... Never the bare four-instrument gate" — names a second, different gate function without linking to it)

src/CLI/Gate.jl:6-20 (`gate(cfg, instruments...; io = stderr) -> Int` — the actual home of the generic closure gate, reached at file #20 of 32 in dependency order, 17 files after its concept was first invoked)
findings.description: The bare word "the gate" / "the closure gate" is used as an already-understood concept starting in the very first substantive docstring a cold reader meets (`DocLints.makedocs`, module #3), long before its home docstring (`CLI/Gate.jl`'s `gate` function, module #20) exists in the read order. Worse, TWO different functions are both named `gate` and both called "the closure gate" in prose: `TestHarness.gate()` (what a consumer's `runtests.jl` calls) and `GBGCodingTools.gate(cfg, instruments...)` (the generic one `TestHarness.gate` calls internally, and that `CLI/Gate.jl` defines and the CLI verb `gbg gate` wraps). `TestHarness.gate`'s own docstring says "Never the bare four-instrument gate" — presupposing the reader already knows there is a separate, more general gate — but never `@ref`-links `GBGCodingTools.gate` to let the reader find it.
findings.resolution_hint: Add an `@ref` from `TestHarness.gate`'s docstring to [`GBGCodingTools.gate`](@ref) at its first mention of "the closure gate of the two code instruments", and from `DocLints.makedocs`'s first mention of "the closure gate" as well; consider naming the two functions distinctly since both being called `gate` and both being called "the closure gate" in prose is the root cause.

findings.title: "lane" is used as settled jargon for 19 modules before any docstring even partially explains it, and no docstring ever states plainly what a lane is
locations: src/CLI/Schema.jl:40-41 (`instrument_schema` docstring, module #5: "the instrument's Workflow `args` object, its lane-file wrapper..." — first use, undefined)
src/Scan.jl:39 (`ScanResult` docstring, module #11: "`note` — ...an error, a dead-lane reason, empty otherwise" — still undefined)

src/CLI/Preflight.jl:223-227,516 (`resolve_checkdocs_lanes` docstring, module #24 — the first place a lane's shape is described at all, and only by listing its constituent keys, never a defining sentence)
findings.description: `lane` first appears in `Schema.jl`'s `instrument_schema` docstring (module #5 of 32 in dependency order) as "its lane-file wrapper", with zero explanation of what a lane is. It recurs undefined through `Scan.jl` (#11), `Sync.jl`/`Init.jl` data strings, `RoundFiles.jl`, `Doctor.jl`, `Gate.jl` before the first descriptive text appears in `Preflight.jl` (#24) — 19 modules later — and even there `resolve_checkdocs_lanes`'s docstring only enumerates what fields a lane record carries (`key`, `kind`, `anchor`, `files`, `brief`), never stating the underlying concept (one agent auditing one surface or territory of an instrument, per the package's own glossary). A reader who stops at any docstring before `Preflight.jl` — which is most of the corpus — has no way to resolve what a "lane" is from the docstrings alone.
findings.resolution_hint: Add a one-clause definition at the first true use (`Schema.jl:instrument_schema`, or better, promote it to the `Scan` or a shared docstring @ref-linked from there): "a lane is one agent's assigned surface or territory within an instrument's round."

findings.title: "hat" and "domain hat" are used for 8 modules before any explanation, and the eventual docstring only lists attributes rather than defining the concept
locations: src/CLI/Init.jl:233 (`init` docstring, module #16: "a placeholder persona for every domain hat without one" — first true docstring use, undefined)
src/CLI/Preflight.jl:181-192 (`resolve_hats` docstring, module #24: "Each hat carries `key`; `substrate`... `anchor`..." — describes fields, never states what a hat conceptually is)
findings.description: `hat` (and the compound `domain hat`) first appears in a real docstring in `CLI/Init.jl`'s `init` (module #16), used as settled jargon — "a placeholder persona for every domain hat without one" — alongside the equally unglossed `persona`. No definition or link is given. The next and only elaboration is `Preflight.resolve_hats`'s docstring 8 modules later (#24), which lists the fields a hat record carries (`key`, `substrate`, `needs`, `anchor`, `persona`, `role`) but never states the underlying concept a cold reader needs — that a hat is one persona in the check-consistency panel, auditing the rendered site from one point of view. A reader stopping anywhere in the first 23 modules has no way to know what a hat is.
findings.resolution_hint: State the concept once at first use (`Init.jl`'s `init` docstring, or promote a one-line definition into `Preflight.resolve_hats` before the field list): "a hat is one persona of the check-consistency panel, reading the rendered site from one point of view."

findings.title: "the ledger" is used bare and unlinked in Reflection.jl two modules before Ledger.jl defines it
locations: src/Reflection.jl:163 (`argcov` docstring, module #8: "The keyword `exempt` is the ledger's `[exemption.match]` predicate" — bare, unlinked, no definition)
src/CLI/Ledger.jl:7-11 (`Ledger` module docstring, module #10: "The reader of a consumer's exemption ledger `.gbg/exemptions.toml`..." — the actual home, reached two modules later)
findings.description: `Reflection.argcov`'s docstring (dependency-order module #8) refers to "the ledger's `[exemption.match]` predicate" as already-known, plain prose with no backtick and no `@ref` link, even though `Ledger` (module #10) — the module that actually explains what a ledger is — has not been read yet by a cold reader proceeding in dependency order. This is a smaller gap than the other findings (two modules, and `Ledger` itself is reasonably self-contained once reached) but is a clean instance of RULE.DOC.XLINK: a cross-module name used before its home, with no qualifying link to let the reader jump there.
findings.resolution_hint: Link the mention: "...is the [`Ledger`](@ref)'s `[exemption.match]` predicate...", per RULE.DOC.XLINK (a cross-module name is `@ref`-linked, qualified, at its first mention).

findings.title: Capitalized "Workflow" is used as a proper-noun package concept throughout but never defined in any docstring
locations: src/CLI/Schema.jl:40 (`instrument_schema` docstring, module #5: "the instrument's Workflow `args` object")
src/CLI/Preflight.jl:9 (`Preflight` module docstring, module #24: "the one renderer of Workflow args")
src/CLI/Rounds.jl:442 (`gbg round rerun` docstring: "prints the instrument's Workflow call")
findings.description: "Workflow" (capitalized, treated as a proper package noun rather than the ordinary English word) recurs across `Schema.jl`, `Preflight.jl`, `Rounds.jl` and elsewhere as though its referent is self-evident — a JS script under `instruments/<name>/workflow/*.js` that a session launches to run the instrument. No docstring in `src/` or `ext/` ever states this. A cold reader can infer from context that it is some kind of callable script object, but the capitalization signals a defined term that is never actually supplied, which is precisely the class of ordinary-word-with-package-meaning that an undefined-symbol check cannot catch (capitalization reads as emphasis, not as an unbound reference).
findings.resolution_hint: Add a one-clause gloss at the first use (`Schema.instrument_schema`, or the `Preflight` module docstring): "a Workflow is the instrument's `workflow/*.js` script, launched by the session that runs the round."
